title: Collect template variable providers from toolchain targets.

timeline.message:
Collect template variable providers from toolchain targets.

They can then be used by rules directly.

Note: genrule does not support per-target toolchains and so this is not
compatible with genrule.

Fixes #5223.

Change-Id: Idf673284a6c91d506e7ed48106050eb10b69f1b6
timeline.author: John Cater

diff.patch:
@@ -998,4 +998,74 @@ EOF
   expect_log 'toolchain extra_str: "bar"'
 }
 
+function test_make_variables_custom_rule() {
+  # Create a toolchain rule that also exposes make variables.
+  mkdir -p toolchain
+  touch toolchain/BUILD
+  cat >> toolchain/toolchain_var.bzl <<EOF
+def _impl(ctx):
+  toolchain = platform_common.ToolchainInfo()
+  value = ctx.attr.value
+  templates = platform_common.TemplateVariableInfo({'VALUE': value})
+  return [toolchain, templates]
+
+toolchain_var = rule(
+    implementation = _impl,
+    attrs = {
+        'value': attr.string(mandatory = True),
+    }
+)
+EOF
+
+  # Create a rule that consumes the toolchain.
+  cat >> toolchain/rule_var.bzl <<EOF
+def _impl(ctx):
+  toolchain = ctx.toolchains['//toolchain:toolchain_var']
+  value = ctx.var['VALUE']
+  print('Using toolchain: value "%s"' % value)
+  return []
+
+rule_var = rule(
+    implementation = _impl,
+    toolchains = ['//toolchain:toolchain_var'],
+)
+EOF
+
+  # Create and register a toolchain
+  cat >> WORKSPACE <<EOF
+register_toolchains('//:toolchain_var_1')
+EOF
+
+  cat >> BUILD <<EOF
+load('//toolchain:toolchain_var.bzl', 'toolchain_var')
+
+# Define the toolchain.
+toolchain_var(
+    name = 'toolchain_var_impl_1',
+    value = 'foo',
+    visibility = ['//visibility:public'])
+
+# Declare the toolchain.
+toolchain(
+    name = 'toolchain_var_1',
+    toolchain_type = '//toolchain:toolchain_var',
+    exec_compatible_with = [],
+    target_compatible_with = [],
+    toolchain = ':toolchain_var_impl_1',
+    visibility = ['//visibility:public'])
+EOF
+
+  # Instantiate the rule and verify the output.
+  mkdir -p demo
+  cat >> demo/BUILD <<EOF
+load('//toolchain:rule_var.bzl', 'rule_var')
+rule_var(name = 'demo')
+EOF
+
+  bazel build //demo:demo &> $TEST_log || fail "Build failed"
+  expect_log 'Using toolchain: value "foo"'
+}
+
+# TODO(katre): Test using toolchain-provided make variables from a genrule.
+
 run_suite "toolchain tests"

What's the significance of "unloaded" in this naming?

reply.body: UnloadedToolchainContext is the class that the ToolchainResolver generates, and the load() method on UnloadedToolchainContext is what is being tested.

timeline.body:
So the [docs](https://docs.bazel.build/versions/master/skylark/lib/platform_common.html#TemplateVariableInfo) describe this as:

> The provider used to retrieve the provider that contains the template variables defined by a particular toolchain

Can you parse this statement for me? We have to go through two providers to get the final info?

reply.body:
That is pretty ugly. Good thing I'm auditing the platform-related documentation this week.

TemplateVariableInfo contains a map of variable names to values, and can be used for automatic make variable expansion (ie, replacing ${FOO} in genrule's cmd, or various other places we handle make var expansion).

timeline.body:
I'm fuzzy on a lot of these themes, so mostly asking for educational clarification and sanity checks:

This continues the theme of pushing make variables into explicitly declared dependencies (toolchains) instead of magical places in the configuration, right?  i.e. this is in line with the make variable refactorings @lberki  has been doing?

is this compatible with @serynth's trimming plans?

Does this specific change add any new power or is it just a preparatory change for genrule integration? If accessing these variables directly through Skylark-defined rules, that power already exists through other (non-template) providers exposed by the toolchain, right?

> This continues the theme of pushing make variables into explicitly declared dependencies (toolchains) instead of magical places in the configuration, right? i.e. this is in line with the make variable refactorings @lberki has been doing?

Yes, exactly. This allows toolchain authors to directly add new make variables that can be expanded, in targets that are using the provided toolchains.

> is this compatible with @serynth's trimming plans?

Yes, it shouldn't have any impact, as it's not changing anything in the configuration directly.

> Does this specific change add any new power or is it just a preparatory change for genrule integration? If accessing these variables directly through Skylark-defined rules, that power already exists through other (non-template) providers exposed by the toolchain, right?

This is something that current toolchain-like rules, such as cc_toolchain and java_toolchain, do already. This change just allows the already-supplied make variables from those targets to be carried forward by the toolchain resolution system.

Rules can currently provide make variables (via TemplateVariableInfo providers) to direct dependencies.
Thanks for all the explanations. lgtm.
